You are a research assistant answering questions about a fixed set of papers.
The papers are plain-text files in your working directory. Explore them with the tools:
- bash: read-only shell (ls, grep -n, find, head, tail, wc, nl, cat, sed -n 'A,Bp')
- read(path, offset, limit): read a file with line numbers

Rules:
- Answer ONLY from text you have actually read in this session. Do not answer from memory.
- If the papers do not contain the answer, say so explicitly instead of guessing.
- When you have enough evidence, reply with your final answer and make NO tool call.
- State only what the document(s) say. Do not add background knowledge, general advice, or your own
  conclusions. If the user asks for something the text only partly covers, answer the covered part
  and say plainly which part the document does not address.
- Do not expand abbreviations, name entities, or add details that the text itself does not give.
- Do not end with a summary that recombines earlier points ("In short", "Overall"); the points stand on their own.
- When the user describes their own situation, say what the document states that applies to it; do not
  draw a personal conclusion that the document does not state itself.

How did the Interim Final Rule change the Head Start rules that govern child safety?

In your answer, refer only to the document in the file `doc.txt`. Do not employ any outside knowledge.

1	47. Before November 30, 2021, Head Start rules (45 C.F.R. § 1302.94(a)) governed volunteer health
     2	only to the following limited extent: (a) A program must ensure regular volunteers have been
     3	screened for appropriate communicable diseases in accordance with state, tribal or local laws. In
     4	the absence of state, tribal or local law, the Health Services Advisory Committee must be consulted
     5	regarding the need for such screenings.
     6	48. But now the Interim Final Rule revises paragraph (a) to read as follows: (a) A program must
     7	ensure volunteers have been screened for appropriate communicable diseases in accordance with state,
     8	tribal or local laws. In the absence of state, tribal, or local law, the Health Services Advisory
     9	Committee must be consulted regarding the need for such screenings. (1) All volunteers in classrooms
    10	or working directly with children other than their own must be fully vaccinated for COVID-19, other
    11	than those volunteers: (i) For whom a vaccine is medically contraindicated; (ii) For whom medical
    12	necessity requires a delay in vaccination; or (iii) Who are legally entitled to an accommodation
    13	with regard to the COVID19 vaccination requirements based on an applicable Federal law. (2) Those
    14	granted an accommodation outlined in paragraph (a)(1) of this section must undergo SARS-CoV-2
    15	testing for current infection at least weekly with those who have negative test results to remain in
    16	the classroom or work directly with children. Those with positive test results must be immediately
    17	excluded from the facility, so they are away from children and staff until they are determined to no
    18	longer be infectious. 86 Fed. Reg. at 68,101.
    19	49. The new paragraphs require volunteers to be vaccinated, and to get tested weekly if granted an
    20	accommodation against being vaccinated. No such requirement existed in the prior version.
    21	50. Before November 30, 2021, Head Start rules (45 C.F.R. § 1302.47(b)(5)) governed child safety
    22	only to the following limited extent: (5) Safety practices. All staff and consultants follow
    23	appropriate practices to keep children safe during all activities, including, at a minimum: (i)
    24	Reporting of suspected or known child abuse and neglect, including that staff comply with applicable
    25	federal, state, local, and tribal laws; (ii) Safe sleep practices, including ensuring that all
    26	sleeping arrangements for children under 18 months of age use firm mattresses or cots, as
    27	appropriate, and for children under 12 months, soft bedding materials or toys must not be used;
    28	(iii) Appropriate indoor and outdoor supervision of children at all times; (iv) Only releasing
    29	children to an authorized adult, and; (v) All standards of conduct described in § 1302.90(c). 9
    30	51. The Interim Final Rule adds paragraph (b)(5)(vi) to read as follows: (vi) Masking, using masks
    31	recommended by CDC, for all individuals 2 years of age or older when there are two or more
    32	individuals in a vehicle owned, leased, or arranged by the Head Start program; indoors in a setting
    33	when Head Start services are provided; and for those not fully vaccinated, outdoors in crowded
    34	settings or during activities that involve sustained close contact with other people, except: (A)
    35	Children or adults when they are either eating or drinking; (B) Children when they are napping; (C)
    36	When a person cannot wear a mask, or cannot safely wear a mask, because of a disability as defined
    37	by the Americans with Disabilities Act; or (D) When a child’s health care provider advises an
    38	alternative face covering to accommodate the child’s special health care needs. 86 Fed. Reg. at
    39	68,101.
    40	52. The new paragraph requires masking. No such requirement existed in the prior version.
    41	53. Paragraph (vi) applies to all “individuals 2 years of age or older” who are “indoors in a
    42	setting when Head Start services are provided” and “outdoors in crowded settings or during
    43	activities that involve sustained close contact with other people” According to the Interim Final
    44	Rule, “The Office of Head Start notes that being outdoors with children inherently includes
    45	sustained close contact for the purposes of caring for and supervising children.” 86 Fed. Reg. at
    46	68,060. Thus, the Mask Mandate appears to also apply to parents who enter a Head Start facility
    47	(either when dropping off or picking up their child or at any other time) and to parents are outside
    48	with their children (either when dropping them off, picking them up, or at any other time), since
    49	being outside with children “inherently includes sustained close contact.”

According to `doc.txt`, the child safety rules are found at 45 C.F.R. § 1302.47(b)(5). Before November 30, 2021, that rule governed child safety only to a limited extent: it required that all staff and consultants follow appropriate practices to keep children safe during all activities, including, at a minimum, (i) reporting of suspected or known child abuse and neglect, (ii) safe sleep practices (firm mattresses or cots for children under 18 months; no soft bedding materials or toys for children under 12 months), (iii) appropriate indoor and outdoor supervision of children at all times, (iv) releasing children only to an authorized adult, and (v) all standards of conduct described in § 1302.90(c).

The Interim Final Rule changed this by adding a new paragraph (b)(5)(vi), which requires masking, using masks recommended by the CDC, for all individuals 2 years of age or older:

- when there are two or more individuals in a vehicle owned, leased, or arranged by the Head Start program;
- indoors in a setting when Head Start services are provided; and
- for those not fully vaccinated, outdoors in crowded settings or during activities that involve sustained close contact with other people.

The new paragraph contains four exceptions: (A) children or adults when eating or drinking; (B) children when napping; (C) when a person cannot wear a mask, or cannot safely wear a mask, because of a disability as defined by the Americans with Disabilities Act; or (D) when a child's health care provider advises an alternative face covering to accommodate the child's special health care needs.

The document states that the new paragraph requires masking and that no such requirement existed in the prior version. It also notes that, because the Office of Head Start stated that being outdoors with children "inherently includes sustained close contact for the purposes of caring for and supervising children," the mask mandate appears to also apply to parents who enter a Head Start facility (e.g., when dropping off or picking up a child) and to parents who are outside with their children.

(The document separately describes a change to the volunteer health rule at 45 C.F.R. § 1302.94(a)—requiring volunteers to be fully vaccinated for COVID-19 or, if granted an accommodation, to undergo weekly SARS-CoV-2 testing—but that is a distinct rule from the child safety rule above.)
